notes: Account: mid-market dev tools company building an IDE copilot integrated into their product and as a hosted extension for customers.
Primary ask: deterministic, reproducible code-completion across releases; ability to pin model version per workspace and to run controlled rollouts/canaries for new model versions.
Latency target: streaming token latency < 50ms median for single-line completions; tail P95 < 200ms for in-editor suggestions.
Throughput: primarly interactive, but spike concurrency during syncs ~200 concurrent editors in a deployment zone.
Cost sensitivity: moderate — willing to pay premium for predictable latency and reproducibility; interested in Optimize recommendations to lower unit cost without hurting quality.
Model preference: open models (LLM-family) with quantized variants for on-prem nodes; want pluggable model catalog and ability to pin exact model digest/hash.
Repro goals: deterministic seeds, stable tokenization, eval gates (unit test prompt sets) that must pass before rollout, and automated rollback on metric regressions.
Security: must support SSO/SAML for developer org, audit logs for generating policy reports, KMS integration for model keys and optional air-gapped packaging for select customers.
Quote from CTO on 2026-03-02 call: 'We need the ability to trace a suggestion back to a pinned model version and an eval snapshot — compliance and debugging are blocking.'

POC: 6-week POC requested — week 1 integration + baseline metrics, week 2 run eval harness, week 3 small canary (5% of traffic), week 4 progressive rollout and monitoring, week 5 failure injection & rollback tests, week 6 handoff and runbook.

POC success criteria: reproducible completions for curated prompt suite, no increase in bug-inducing suggestions (measured via internal lint/regression tests), latency within targets under 90th percentile of expected load.
Existing infra: Kubernetes clusters in GCP with an internal discovery service; CI runs nightly integration tests that must incorporate Redwood eval results.
Integration asks: SDK hooks for seeding and provenance metadata on completions, per-workspace model pinning UI, canary API that routes X% of requests to new model variant and collects eval metrics.
Metrics they will watch: suggestion accuracy (developer-accepted rate), revert rate (how often a suggestion is modified), latency P50/P95, token cost per session, and security audit events.

Requested features from Redwood: immutable model identifiers, rollout policies (canary + staged), eval gates integrated with CI, automated rollback thresholds, traceable request -> model mapping in logs.
Notes on fallback behavior: prefer graceful degradation to smaller, faster quantized model vs complete failure; want automatic route to hosted low-cost fallback for unrecognized workflows.

Competitive concerns: using OpenAI currently for prod; evaluating Redwood for better deployment control and reproducibility. Primary tie-breaker: can Redwood provide pinned model digests and deterministic outputs for compliance?
Internal stakeholders: CTO (decision), Head of Product (UX for model pinning), Lead SRE (onboarding and SLA), Security lead (compliance).
Budget: headcount + infra commit; procurement will require a one-time integration budget plus annual reserved capacity if Dedicated chosen. Finance expects preliminary TCO estimates by POC end.
